PullRequest.Title: sessions: Show per-chat state in the sessions list
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

- show each expanded peer chat's modified time, activity, and unread state in the Sessions list
- keep the expanded parent row scoped to the main chat while projecting aggregate child progress and unread state when collapsed
- mark the specific chat read when it is opened, with session-level fallback for providers without chat-scoped read state
- propagate Agent Host chat-local activity and modification timestamps, and reconcile local read state with newer protocol updates

Nested chats previously inherited or omitted aggregate session metadata, so peer activity and timestamps could be stale or absent and opening a peer did not clear its unread state.

## Reviewer notes

Agent Host does not currently expose a client-dispatchable chat-read protocol action. The provider therefore keeps an opened chat's read state locally until newer activity or an explicit protocol read-state transition supersedes it.

## Validation

- `npm run compile` — passed
- `npm run hygiene` — passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsList.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/services/sessions/test/browser/sessionsManagementService.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/services/sessions/test/browser/sessionNavigation.test.ts` — 451 passing, 2 pending
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostStateManager.test.ts` — 110 passing
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts --grep "multi-chat catalog|observing the main chat modified time holds"` — 49 passing

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed observer, provider wrapper, reference collection, IPC subscription call, 30-second retention, and prior payload-only listing path are all directly traced in code. Exact user counts and restore duration are uncertain, which limits severity, but the per-unique-row fan-out mechanism is deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: one live Agent Host session-state IPC subscription plus restored per-session state/database objects for each distinct rendered row
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cold work grows with the number of distinct Agent Host session rows rendered while opening or scrolling the Sessions list; subscriptions are coalesced per session across fields, but unique rows remain retained for the 30-second idle window, so fast scrolling can exceed viewport cardinality.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: excessive IPC, Agent Host restore/database I/O, process CPU and retained memory, with degraded Sessions-list responsiveness
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The row read `session.updatedAt` and `session.description`, which the provider projects from the verified listing payload without opening the per-session database or subscribing to each session URI.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The row now selects `mainChat.updatedAt` for every single-chat session (and main-chat description/read state on the same scope). This PR also wraps those main-chat observables in `_withChatDetails`, whose first observer calls `_ensureSessionStateSubscription` and `connection.getSubscription(StateComponents.Session, ...)`.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The diff replaces the prior `element.updatedAt.read(reader)` row read with `getSessionRowUpdatedAt(...)`, whose added RIGHT line 296 reads `session.mainChat.updatedAt`; in the same diff, `mainChat.updatedAt` changes from the summary observable to `_withChatDetails(defaultChatUpdatedAt)`. Thus the list newly crosses the session-subscription boundary for each single-chat row, whereas it did not before.
Findings.Title: Keep single-chat rows on summary-backed metadata
Findings.Impact: Opening or scrolling a history containing many Agent Host sessions now creates a burst of per-session subscriptions and can restore every encountered session even though the user only asked to view the summary list. Each row leaves its underlying subscription alive for 30 seconds after recycling, so scrolling through dozens of rows can keep dozens of restored sessions live.
Findings.Evidence: `isSessionRowMainChatScoped` returns true whenever `session.chats.length <= 1`, independent of collapse state, and line 296 observes `mainChat.updatedAt` from the ordinary session-row renderer and accessibility label. In `AgentHostSessionAdapter`, this PR changes `mainChat.updatedAt`, `isRead`, and `description` to `_withChatDetails(...)`; `_withChatDetails` acquires `_sessionChatDetailsReferences`, whose first reference calls `_ensureSessionStateSubscription`. That method issues `connection.getSubscription(StateComponents.Session, ...)`, and its own comment notes that subscribing can trigger Agent Host restore; the provider documentation states listing payload projection otherwise avoids opening each per-session database.
Findings.Recommendation: For single-chat and collapsed rows, continue rendering summary-backed session fields (`session.updatedAt`, `session.description`, and `session.isRead`), which are equivalent to the only chat without requiring hydration. Acquire chat-detail observables only for an explicitly expanded multi-chat session (or add the default-chat timestamp to summary metadata if it can genuinely differ).

Scenarios.Scenario: Open and scroll the Sessions list containing Agent Host history
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session rows render synchronously from the listing facade, but the newly observed main-chat fields acquire session-state subscriptions during row observation. The subscription response is not awaited for initial DOM paint, yet Agent Host restoration and subsequent observable updates run concurrently and contend with list interaction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold IPC subscription per distinct rendered Agent Host session, coalesced across updatedAt/isRead/description observers for the same session but not across different sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Rows consumed `session.updatedAt`, `session.description`, and session read state from listing metadata, so ordinary list rendering did not subscribe to every session URI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not awaited by initial paint, but creates an unbounded cross-session burst of host work and later UI updates while the user opens or scrolls the list.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore/materialize per-session state and its database as a consequence of subscribing to the session channel
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one cold restore for each unique session subscribed while scrolling; warm/materialized sessions avoid repeated restoration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Verified payload listing projected row metadata without opening each per-session database.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs transitively after the IPC subscription and can add disk/CPU/memory contention even though initial row paint does not await completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct Agent Host session rows rendered while the list is open, including rows visited by scrolling during the 30-second idle-retention window; effective cardinality is one subscription per unique session after per-session reference coalescing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each row acquires synchronously, while unique session subscription/restore requests can be in flight together without a cross-session limiter. Multiple fields and observers for one session coalesce through the reference collection and connection subscription cache.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm sessions reuse `_sessionStateSubscriptions` or an existing active-chat subscription. Cold rows issue a subscription; when the row is recycled, the underlying subscription remains for 30 seconds. Failed subscriptions are deliberately not cached and may retry on later observation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed row helper, `_withChatDetails` wrapper, reference collection, subscription call, restoration warning, and idle lifecycle are all explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of visible/scrolled rows and restore cost vary by history size, machine, and warm state; this affects severity, not the directly traced fan-out mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity boundary fan-out; keep single-chat/collapsed rows on summary-backed metadata and reserve detail subscriptions for explicitly expanded multi-chat state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an unread main or peer chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Navigation opens the selected chat and invokes chat-scoped read marking. Provider completion is not awaited by the list open callback; the SessionsService reaction may then clear aggregate session unread state when all non-archived chats are read.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Optional provider `setChatReadState`, and `setSessionReadState` when aggregate unread clears
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one chat-scoped call per navigation plus one session-scoped call when that navigation clears the final unread chat; Agent Host multi-chat marking is local and only the aggregate session update crosses its protocol boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening an unread active session made one session-level read-state call and had no chat-scoped operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Calls are fire-and-report-error on navigation and do not block opening the chat.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected chat per user navigation; aggregate-read evaluation scans the chats in the active session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No collection burst from one open. Agent Host mutates multi-chat local read state synchronously; providers with remote chat-scoped read APIs may have one request in flight, followed by one session-level request only when the final unread chat is cleared.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Read state is observable provider state rather than a cache. Agent Host local overrides persist until newer protocol activity or an explicit protocol read transition; no repeated cold lookup is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for call count and non-blocking placement; transport cost varies by provider.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider implementations may use IPC or network transport, but the changed cardinality is bounded to explicit navigation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No report: the extra operation is bounded to an explicit open, preserves chat-scoped semantics, and does not fan out with session history.

Scenarios.Scenario: Receive Agent Host chat status, activity, or modification updates
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Every chat action is reduced in AgentHostStateManager; changed chat-local summary fields now dispatch a `SessionChatUpdated` envelope to session subscribers before aggregate summary reconciliation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Deliver `SessionChatUpdated` to clients subscribed to that session channel
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one additional session-channel envelope for each action that changes chat-local status, activity, or modifiedAt, multiplied by subscribed clients; streamed markdown deltas do not change modifiedAt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The session-channel patch was emitted only for status changes; aggregate root summary updates already carried session-level state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs inline with action dispatch but carries a small patch and is limited to subscribed sessions.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Actual chat lifecycle/activity events. `modifiedAt` changes at turn start/end in the reducer rather than on every streamed `ChatDelta`; activity frequency is producer-driven.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Dispatch is synchronous per action and ordered on the channel. There is no new cross-chat Promise burst; delivery fans out only to existing subscribers.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Only changed status/activity/modifiedAt fields are emitted. Equal values suppress the new session-channel action; subscribers already share channel state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for event gating and ordering.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Activity event frequency depends on the agent producer, but reducer evidence rules out per-token modified-time traffic.
Scenarios.Verdict: No report: the added event propagation is change-gated, small, and not on the token-streaming path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render expanded peer-chat rows with activity, markdown, unread state, and relative time
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Visible virtualized rows synchronously rebuild their details DOM and, when needed, render a plaintext-sanitized markdown status. Each non-compact rendered chat row owns a one-minute relative-time interval.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of simultaneously rendered peer rows, bounded by tree virtualization and viewport height; timers scale with rendered rows, not the full session catalog.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: DOM work is synchronous per rendered row. Timer callbacks run once per minute per rendered row; recycled rows dispose their intervals and markdown renderers.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cross-row cache is added. Row disposal clears timers and rendered markdown; the associated session-detail subscription is coalesced per owning session.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from renderer ownership and element-disposable cleanup.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large viewports and unusually dense expanded sessions increase visible-row count, but the work remains viewport-bounded and minute-cadenced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No report: added synchronous rendering is bounded by virtualization, and timer/markdown lifecycles are cleaned up when rows recycle.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 20 changed files and all diff pages. Reported one introduced Agent Host boundary-fanout regression: ordinary single-chat list rows now observe detail-backed fields and open per-session state subscriptions. Other changed rendering, read-state, and event-propagation paths were bounded or coalesced and did not meet the reporting threshold.
